clue.text: Parking by lake in Harrow?

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
an Irish word for a lake

explanation.surface: Someone is looking for somewhere to leave the car beside a lake in Harrow, the London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow looks like the London district (and its school); it is the farm implement. A lough is an Irish lake, as in Lough Neagh.
explanation.definitionFit: A harrow and a plough are both farm tools dragged over a field to break up soil, so one serves as an example of the other.

clue.text: Rex lodged in terrible rooms

indicators.note: a lodger lives inside someone else's home, so one word goes within another

blocks.note: parlous means dangerously bad
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A man called Rex is a lodger in some awful rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex looks like a name; it is the Latin for king, as in the royal signature.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlours are sitting rooms, especially in older houses, kept for receiving guests.

clue.text: Literary character visiting brothel, lovelorn

indicators.note: a visitor is inside the place they call on, so the word sits within the clue words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A lovelorn figure from a book calls at a brothel.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the Moorish general in Shakespeare's tragedy, a famous character from literature, himself tormented by love.

clue.text: Made up with good boy

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a boy is a lad

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted with their well-behaved son.
explanation.walkthrough: Made up is informal British (especially northern) for delighted, not invented or wearing make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad means pleased, which is what the colloquial British phrase made up expresses.

clue.text: Flight impressed head of EasyJet

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: impressed as with a seal or die
the opening letter of the airline's name

explanation.surface: A pun on airline flights: a passenger was impressed by the boss of EasyJet, the budget carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: Flight looks like an aeroplane journey, matching EasyJet; here it means fleeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a panicked rush of animals or people running away, which is a flight in the sense of escape.

clue.text: I don't believe it is what a child could say after a bedtime story

definitions.text: what a child could say after a bedtime story

blocks.note: first meaning: a sceptical retort to a tall tale

blocks.clueFragment: what a child could say after a bedtime story
blocks.note: second meaning: a plea for one more tale before sleep

explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase is sarcastic in one reading and a literal request in the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses disbelief, while a sleepy youngster asking for one more tale uses the very same words literally.

clue.text: Short Girl Guide's bad behaviour

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

blocks.note: a miss is a girl
to guide is to conduct, as with a tour

explanation.surface: A small member of the Girl Guides has been misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Girl Guide reads as one organisation (the British equivalent of Girl Scouts) but splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Misconduct is improper or unacceptable behaviour, especially by someone in a professional role.

clue.text: English male meeting one judge in Abu Dhabi?

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
M is the abbreviation for male
the Roman numeral for one
to judge is to rate or assess

explanation.surface: An Englishman meets a judge in the Gulf city of Abu Dhabi.
explanation.walkthrough: Abu Dhabi looks like the place of the meeting; it is the definition, by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is one of the seven states of the United Arab Emirates, ruled by an emir, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Plantation close to jungle, say

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of jungle
to say is to state

explanation.surface: Someone describes a plantation as lying near the jungle.
explanation.walkthrough: Close to reads as near; it means the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a large area of land growing a crop such as tea or rubber, which is a plantation.

clue.text: Tries in proper practice session

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other, sitting within it

blocks.note: proper as in genuine
a judge tries, or hears, a case in court

explanation.surface: Rugby players score tries in a proper training session.
explanation.walkthrough: Tries suggests rugby scores or attempts; it is the legal sense, a court hearing a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a run-through of a performance before the real thing, a session for practice.

clue.text: One providing technical support may show new line with eagerness

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so these letters are given a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A helpdesk worker shows real eagerness about a new product line.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales engineer is a technical specialist who supports a sales team by advising customers on how a product works.

clue.text: Wading bird, last in this list

indicators.note: the last in a word is its closing letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the closing letter of this
a ship that lists leans to one side, or tilts

explanation.surface: Someone reading a list of wading birds notes which comes at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: List looks like a catalogue of birds, but it is the verb for a ship leaning over.
explanation.definitionFit: The stilt is a long-legged black-and-white wading bird of shallow waters.

clue.text: Duck on very large lake in capital

blocks.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize
L is the map abbreviation for lake
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, the shape of O

explanation.surface: A duck paddles on a very large lake in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'Duck on' the rest means the duck's letter is placed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Colourful chap hiding lad in apartment

indicators.note: something that hides another holds it out of sight inside
one word is placed inside the other, sitting within it

blocks.note: the British word for an apartment
a chap is a man
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A colourful character is hiding a young lad in his apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the boy goes inside the man, and that pair goes inside the flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant means showy and vivid, so a colourful personality or outfit can be called that.

clue.text: Camaraderie in chap's joint

blocks.note: a chap is a fellow, plus the S of the possessive
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: Good comradeship can be found in a man's favourite bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Joint suggests a pub or club; it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellowship is friendly companionship among people sharing interests, the same as camaraderie.

clue.text: Chicken dish ordered is cooked across most of country

indicators.note: food that is cooked is transformed from its raw state, so these letters change order
most of a word is all but its final letter, so the tail is dropped
letters spread across another word straddle it, holding it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a country is a land

explanation.surface: In a restaurant, a chicken dish that has been ordered is being cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the letters to be rearranged; 'is cooked' does the signalling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhode Island Red is a well-known American breed of domestic chicken with reddish-brown feathers.

clue.text: Henry, entertaining German theologian, makes a warming drink

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests has them inside, so one thing is held within another

blocks.note: Hy is the old written abbreviation of the name Henry
a typical German man's name
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: Henry is hosting a German religious scholar and serves him a hot drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot toddy is whisky mixed with hot water, honey and lemon, drunk to warm up or ease a cold.

clue.text: Role played with conviction in musical work

indicators.note: something played is performed in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor performs a part with real conviction in a musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A violin concerto is a composition for solo violin and orchestra, a substantial piece of music.

clue.text: To kill, you need to choose a murder weapon?

blocks.note: slang for murdering someone
to choose is to pick

explanation.surface: A would-be murderer is told to pick a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is because an ice pick is a tool for breaking ice, though it famously killed Trotsky.
explanation.definitionFit: Leon Trotsky was assassinated with this mountaineering tool, so it can serve as an example of a weapon used for killing.

clue.text: Put out in seldom encountered joy

indicators.note: out as in disordered or put out of place, so the letters are mixed
one word is placed inside the other, sitting within it

blocks.note: something seldom met is rare
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed at being disturbed amid a rare moment of happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: Put out reads as one phrasal verb meaning annoyed; split, the first word is the letters and the second the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapture is a state of intense delight, an extreme form of joy.

clue.text: County Durham's top store vandalised

indicators.note: the top of a down entry's word is its first letter
something vandalised is smashed up, so these letters are wrecked into a new order

blocks.note: the opening letter of Durham
taken as written

explanation.surface: A news item: in County Durham, the best shop in town has been vandalised.
explanation.walkthrough: County Durham reads as one place name, but County is the definition and Durham only gives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is a county on the south coast of England.

clue.text: Finished last in row - crew too heavy?

indicators.note: the last in a word is its closing letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: finished, as in done
the closing letter of row
a rowing crew of eight oarsmen is called an eight

explanation.surface: A rowing team that came last wonders whether its crew was too heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: Row here is the oarsman's verb in the surface; in the wordplay it just supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Overweight describes something above the proper or healthy weight, which is being too heavy.

clue.text: Notice a pimple

blocks.note: first meaning: to see or catch sight of
second meaning: a small blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone looking in the mirror sees a blemish on their face.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for catching sight of something and as a noun for a small skin blemish.

clue.text: Primate drawing in small recess

indicators.note: drawing something in pulls it inside, so one part is enclosed by another

blocks.note: an ape is a primate
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A monkey is sketching in a little alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: Primate also suggests an archbishop, which fits the church setting of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess at the end of a church, usually behind the altar.

clue.text: Smart son to bid

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to bid someone well is to wish them well

explanation.surface: A smart son is going to make a bid at an auction.
explanation.walkthrough: Bid looks like an auction offer; it is the older sense, as in bidding someone farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal British for smart or fashionable, as in a swish hotel.

clue.text: Poet's book, 20/-

blocks.note: Ezra is a book of the Old Testament
20/- is twenty shillings in old British money, which made one pound

explanation.surface: A poet's book is priced at twenty shillings.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British money had twenty shillings to the pound, written 20/-.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra Pound was an American modernist writer of verse, author of the Cantos.

clue.text: Get hold of some and join in

blocks.note: to get hold of something is to take it
some of something is part of it

explanation.surface: An invitation to grab a share and get involved.
explanation.definitionFit: To take part is to participate in an activity, joining in with others.

clue.text: Amateur substituted by me in game gets treatment

indicators.note: a thing substituted by another is swapped out and replaced in the same spot

blocks.note: game in the sense of willing, as in I'm game
A is the abbreviation for amateur, as in AAA
taken as written

explanation.surface: An amateur player is replaced by the speaker in a match, and receives treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: Game looks like a sport but means willing.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a cure or medicine, the treatment given for an illness.
